info.description:
**Threat Scenario Generator (TSG) | Remedation | Service Mapper.

**Who is calling.** Every call in groups 5-9 and 11 sends four headers: `X-API-Key` (from group 2),
`X-User-Id`, `X-Entity-Id` (a number) and `X-Tenant-Id`. Groups 2, 3 and 10 send `X-Admin-Key` instead.
Groups 1 and 4 need no key.

**Long work runs in the background.** A start answers 202 with an id; poll its status (or open its live
updates, group 9) until it is done. Errors come as `application/problem+json`: `code`, `detail`, and a
`reason` on a 409.
info.title: DESC - Critical Information Infrastructure

get.description: Answers `{"status": "ok"}` while the process runs (the liveness probe). No key.

200 `ready` when MongoDB answers, else 503 `not_ready`. Redis, SQL Server and live workers per queue
are reported but never fail readiness: each serves only some routes, and a 503 here would take every
route out of service. No key.
get.summary: 2. Are its stores and workers ready?

get.description:
Every job of every kind (runs, plans, service mappings, intelligence refreshes, embeddings builds)
active in the last `hours`, newest first: status (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), the retry it
waits for, its error, the worker running it. `queues`: each queue's waiting messages and workers online.
Filter by `module` (threat_scenarios, remediation, service_mapper, external_intelligence,
library_embeddings, maintenance), `status` (repeatable), `kind` (a task name such as tsg_map_services,
or an admin job kind) and `request_id` (the X-Request-Id of the call that queued it).

Any job by its id (an import's or build's job_id, or a run's, plan's or mapping's id): its module,
status, error, retry and worker. 404 for an unknown id.

post.description:
Queued: it never starts. Running: an import stops at its next NVD request or source, keeping what it
read (the next import continues from there); a build finishes but its outcome is dropped. The job reads
`cancelled`, a new one of its kind can start at once, and the cancel is audited. 409 `nothing_to_cancel`
for a job already ended or another module's job (a run or plan has its own cancel).
post.summary: Cancel an intelligence import or embeddings build

post.description:
A background build: 202 `{job_id}`. One at a time (409 `job_in_progress`, `details.job_id`). Needed
once after the library is loaded; later builds run by themselves.
post.summary: 1. Build the library's search vectors now

get.description: Its `status`: queued, running, then done or failed (with `error`).

Every run's current scenarios of the entity, newest first; `decision` filters (pending, accepted,
rejected). The entity must be the caller's (`X-Entity-Id`), else 403.

Every plan of the entity, newest first, filtered as a run's list. The entity must be the caller's
(X-Entity-Id), else 403.
My entity's runs, plans and service mappings that are queued or running, oldest first.

post.description:
Start writing a remediation plan for one scenario: v1's one request for both kinds.

- **is_manual=false**: send `session_id` and `scenario_id` of an ACCEPTED scenario of that run.
- **is_manual=true**: send `manual_scenario` (a scenario a person wrote) and an `Idempotency-Key` header.
  TSG saves the scenario, accepts it and plans it. The same key and body again: 200, `replayed: true`;
  if that plan failed for an outage (`error.code` `unavailable`), its version is written again: 202.

Every other field is the register's data; all are optional. `supporting_systems_applicable_to_risk` names
the asset's systems the risk applies to (none: the asset itself), and
`supporting_systems_applicable_to_existing_controls` those the existing controls are on (none: no
system). Answers 202 at once with `remediation_id`, `session_id` and `scenario_id`: keep the last two,
because every later call on the plan takes them in its address. No AI is called here: the plan job
matches the scenario's controls (and a hand-written one's attacker) if they are missing, then writes the
plan; poll `GET .../treatment-plan/status` until `latest_status` is `done`.

Errors: 404 scenario unknown or not in that run; 403 another entity's; 409 `scenario_not_accepted`,
`plan_already_exists` (regenerate it instead), `idempotency_key_conflict`, `control_library_empty`,
`run_being_deleted`; 422 a field, the two kinds mixed, or a listed system that is not a supporting
system of the scenario's asset.

202 starts generation 1. The same Idempotency-Key and body answer 200 with that mapping, or 202 with a
new try when the key's generation is still the latest and failed for an outage (`error.code`
`unavailable`).

Send `{"accept": [dependency_id, ...], "reject": [...]}`; either list may be null or empty. The valid
ids are saved together; `failed` lists each id that was not, and why. 409 until the mapping is `done`:
regenerate a `failed` one.

202 starts the next generation of a `done` or `failed` mapping (409 `generation_in_progress` while one
runs). The same Idempotency-Key answers 200 with the generation it started, or 202 with a new try when
that generation is still the latest and failed for an outage (`error.code` `unavailable`).

get.description:
Poll until `progress.overall` is no longer `generating`: `done` (decide the relationships;
`progress.relationships` counts them), `failed` (`error` says why) or `cancelled`.

post.description:
Send `asset_id` and `supporting_system_id` (one id or a list; `service_id`, `sector_id`,
`subsector_id` optional). 202 with the run's status; keep `session_id`. With an `Idempotency-Key`
header a retry is safe (the same key and body: 200, the same run). 409 `intel_no_data`: external
intelligence is on but nothing is imported yet (group 4).

delete.description:
Deletes the run, its scenarios and their plans; it cannot be undone. 409 `cancel_first` while its
work runs.

get.description:
Poll until `progress.overall` says what to do: `awaiting_review` (group 6), `awaiting_next_set`,
`complete`, `error` or `cancelled`. Each stage (threats, scenarios, controls) reads PENDING,
RUNNING, COMPLETE or ERROR.

post.description:
Send `{"mode": "subset", "scenario_ids": ["..."]}`, `{"mode": "all"}` or `{"mode": "none"}` (decides
nothing), as TSG v1 does; `replace_accepted: true` (optional, with subset) lets a newer version replace an
accepted one. The v2 body is also accepted: `{"scenario_ids": ["..."]}` or `{"scenario_ids": "all"}`. An
accepted scenario can get a remediation plan (group 7).

v1_replace.summary: Accept a newer version in place of the accepted one (v1)

post.description:
Stops the run's work; what is already written stays readable. 409 `nothing_to_cancel` when
nothing runs.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events: `session.updated` (the body of `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}`) now and at
every change; `session.deleted` once when it is deleted. Swagger cannot show a stream: use
`curl -N` or a browser EventSource.

Why the run has as many scenarios as it has: how many candidates each planning stage took in and let
out (`counts`; a slot is one threat as one kind of attack), each candidate left out with its stage,
reason and detail (`drops`, the most telling first), and what became of the planned paths (`writing`:
written, still to write, given up and why). 404 before the run is planned.
get.summary: 6. How a run's plan was made

post.description:
Send `{"scenario_ids": ["..."]}`: each is written again in the background (202); follow it with
`GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}`. The earlier version stays readable (`include_replaced=true`). A card
that failed because the AI did not answer is written again in its place.

get.description:
The written scenarios: threat, actors, systems, evidence and controls. `include_replaced=true` adds
the versions a regenerate replaced. Paged with `offset` and `limit`.

post.description:
Writes more scenarios from the attack paths not written yet (202). 409 `nothing_left` when every
path is written.
Send `{"scenario_ids": ["..."]}`. Each answer row says what was done or why not.

get.description: One scenario of the run, in full.

post.description:
For an accepted scenario whose threat the AI proposed: it goes to the curators as pending
(group 10), never straight into the library.
post.summary: 5. Propose an AI-written threat to the library

get.description:
The result: the plan shown (the accepted version, else the newest finished one), its warnings, the
scenario it treats and the register's data (v2's old `.../result`, at v1's address).
`include_history=true` adds every version with its own decision.

post.description: Stops the version being written (409 `nothing_to_cancel` when none is). Regenerate writes it again.

get.description:
The plan's status now (`remediation.updated`: the body of `.../treatment-plan/status`), then every
change, until the client closes; `remediation.deleted` once, when its run is deleted.

post.description:
Send `{}`: the next version (2, 3, ...) is written from the same register data and the scenario's
current controls; the earlier versions stay. Follow it with `.../status`, then accept the one you want:
`.../review {"decision": "accepted", "version": 2}`. Allowed once the latest version is done, failed or
cancelled; 409 `generation_in_progress` before that. A latest version that failed for an outage
(`error.code` `unavailable`) is written again instead: the same version number, so it uses no version and
the version limit (409 `version_limit_reached`) does not stop it.
post.summary: 5. Regenerate: write a new version (v2, v3...)

post.description:
v1's review call: `{"decision": "accepted"}` or `"rejected"`, for `version` (leave it out for the
newest finished one), with an optional `comment`. Accepting a version makes it THE plan; repeating a
decision changes nothing. 409 `not_complete` while the version is still being written.

get.description:
The cheap poll: `latest_status` queued → running → done (or failed / cancelled), the review `decision`
(pending, accepted, rejected) and `progress.overall`, which says what to do next (generating,
awaiting_review, accepted, rejected, failed, cancelled; read_only when no version is decided and the
scenario is no longer accepted, so it cannot be reviewed). 404 when the scenario has no plan.
Every plan of the run's scenarios, newest first, filtered by `status`, `decision` or `risk_level`.
Every client's id, name and state (`?active=true` or `false`); never a key.

post.description:
Send `{"name": "shield-frontend", "description": "..."}` with `X-Admin-Key`. The answer holds
`api_key` ONCE: keep it; every caller sends it as `X-API-Key`. 201.
The key stops working at once; the client stays listed as revoked.

get.description:
Each source's state, the active `snapshot_id` (set once data is imported and indexed: runs need it),
`stale`, `pending_sources`, `no_data`, and the evidence settings (reranker, threshold).

post.description:
A background import, 202 `{job_id}`: every source that is due (all 6 the first time), or one with
`{"source": "cisa_kev"}`. Needed by hand only the first time; then it runs every hour by itself. 409 while
the switch is off, or while an import runs (`details.job_id` names it); 422 an unknown or withdrawn
source.

get.description: Poll until `status` is `done` (or `failed`, with `error`); then check the health (5).

post.description:
It starts empty and an import of it is queued (`refresh_job_id`; null when one already runs or the
switch is off). 409 while the env file switches the feature off.

Audited first; then the source's records and vectors are deleted and it is no longer imported.
Scenarios already written keep what they cite.
post.summary: 6. Withdraw a source and delete its data

get.description:
`env_enabled`: the env file's EXTERNAL_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED; `runtime_enabled`: this switch;
`effective`: both on, so the feeds are imported and new scenarios cite them.

put.description:
`{"enabled": false}`: no more hourly imports, imports by hand are refused, new scenarios are written
without the feeds; nothing is deleted. `{"enabled": true}`: back on, and an import starts. Audited.
409 while the env file says EXTERNAL_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED=false (only the env file and a restart change
that).

Send `{"approve": [512], "reject": [513]}` (pending ids). An approved row joins the live library;
a rejected one is never proposed again.
